At least 1 year of recent experience working in environment with loading/unloading heavy items and/or sanitation.
This position involves keeping ULAR animal facilities supplied with clean animal cages (that can weigh around 4
pounds each). Incumbent will need to load cage racks with 144-plus animal cages, and push the racks through
tunnel washers for washing. Some of the cages need to be sterilized through autoclave which also need to be
loaded and unloaded.
Once the cages and racks are washed, incumbent will prepare the cages for use by putting bedding and feed in
the cages. Once prepared, hundreds of cages are loaded onto metal bulk trucks and transported to animal
housing rooms. Incumbents will also need to move animal feed and bedding, with each bag weighing 50 pounds.
Incumbent will be responsible for cleaning and minor repairs of cage enclosures and related ancillary equipment.
ULAR will provide the necessary training to perform these duties.
Able to lift, push, pull and move items weighing up to 50 pounds.
May be required to work weekends and holidays on rotation.
Must wear protective clothing provided by ULAR (scrubs, masks, gloves, shoe covers, etc).
Must attend technician training courses/meetings per ULAR’s discretion.

Must participate in medical monitoring programs as prescribed by the Occupational Health and Safety Program. This may include preventive medical programs such as TB screening, tetanus booster, blood testing, immunizations, medical surveillance and others to meet the state, federal and UC requirements.

Must be comfortable working alone in following conditions: constant exposure to possible allergens, including but not limited to animal waste, dirty bedding, animal hair, dander, dust, steam, in an enclosed, confined area with no direct access to open air.
Ability to function effectively as a team member.
Ability to read, write and understand English sufficiently in order to follow given instructions and written standard operating procedures.
